Patch series ""mm: memcontrol: memory.stat cost & correctness"".
The cgroup memory.stat file holds recursive statistics for the entire
subtree.  The current implementation does this tree walk on-demand
whenever the file is read.  This is giving us problems in production.
1. The cost of aggregating the statistics on-demand is high.  A lot of
system service cgroups are mostly idle and their stats don't change
between reads
column2: yet we always have to check them.  There are also always

column1: some lazily-dying cgroups sitting around that are pinned by a handful
of remaining page cache; the same applies to them.
In an application that periodically monitors memory.stat in our
fleet
column2: we have seen the aggregation consume up to 5% CPU time.

column1: 2. When cgroups die and disappear from the cgroup tree
accumulated vm events.  The result is that the event counters at
higher-level cgroups can go backwards and confuse some of our
automation
column2: let alone people looking at the graphs over time.

column1: To address both issues
column2: this patch series changes the stat

column1: implementation to spill counts upwards when the counters change.
The upward spilling is batched using the existing per-cpu cache.  In a
sparse file stress test with 5 level cgroup nesting
of the flushing was negligible (a little under 1% of CPU at 100% CPU
utilization
column2: compared to the 5% of reading memory.stat during regular

column1: operation).
This patch (of 4):
memcg_page_state()
currently returning the state of the local memcg or lruvec
recursive state.
In practice there is a demand for both versions
that want the recursive counts currently sum them up by hand.
Per default
column2: cgroups are considered recursive entities and generally we

column1: expect more users of the recursive counters
special cases.  To reflect that in the name
current implementations.
The following patch will re-incarnate these functions with recursive
semantics
